今治焼豚玉子飯.summary: A local dish of Imabari: rice topped with thin slices of roast pork and a soft fried egg, drizzled with a sweet and savory sauce. It is said to have started as a staff meal at a Chinese restaurant in Imabari. The classic way is to break the runny yolk and mix it with the pork and sauce, and the silky egg and sauce-soaked rice go perfectly together. Quick to eat and filling, it has been loved by locals. Many shops in Imabari serve it, and it is known nationwide.

shops.name: Hakurakuten Imabari
shops.query: 白楽天 今治本店
shops.comment: The Chinese restaurant where yakibuta tamagomeshi was born.

shops.name: Shigematsu Hanten
shops.query: 重松飯店 今治
shops.comment: A popular spot for yakibuta tamagomeshi.

今治焼き鳥.summary: Imabari's yakitori is cooked on an iron griddle instead of on skewers. Pressing the meat down with a weight on the griddle lets excess fat drain off and makes the surface crisp and fragrant. Chicken skin is especially popular, with an addictive crunch. One story says it was devised to cook faster for Imabari's impatient people. Imabari is also known for having many yakitori restaurants for its population. Pair it with sightseeing along the Shimanami Kaido.

shops.name: Yakitori Yamadori
shops.query: やきとり 山鳥 今治
shops.comment: A well-known Imabari yakitori shop using Iyo Suigun-dori chicken.

shops.name: Maruki Matsumoto
shops.query: 丸起 松本店 今治 焼き鳥
shops.comment: A popular shop for griddle-cooked Imabari yakitori.

八幡浜ちゃんぽん.summary: Local champon of Yawatahama. It features a light, golden broth made from chicken bones, bonito and kelp, lighter than Nagasaki champon. It is loaded with vegetables such as cabbage, bean sprouts and carrot, plus pork, kamaboko and the local jakoten fish cake. It has long been loved by locals in the port town of Yawatahama. The city has many shops, each with its own flavor. Enjoy it together with jakoten.

shops.name: Maruyama Chanpon
shops.query: 丸山ちゃんぽん 八幡浜
shops.comment: A postwar shop said to be the originator of Yawatahama chanpon.

shops.name: Agora Marche
shops.query: アゴラマルシェ 八幡浜 フードコート
shops.comment: Try chanpon at the roadside station's food court.

三津浜焼き.summary: Local okonomiyaki of Mitsuhama, a port district of Matsuyama. A thin crepe of batter is layered with cabbage, noodles, minced beef fat and chikuwa, then folded in half at the end. It is half-moon shaped and eaten with plenty of sweet sauce. Using beef fat gives it a rich flavor. Old-fashioned okonomiyaki shops are scattered around Mitsuhama. Enjoy it along with a stroll through the retro streets. Its homey taste is a delight.

shops.name: Okonomiyaki Miyoshi
shops.query: お好み焼き みよし 三津浜
shops.comment: A long-running shop that represents Mitsuhama-yaki.

shops.name: Hinode
shops.query: 日の出 三津浜焼き 松山
shops.comment: A popular Mitsuhama-yaki shop.

宇和島鯛めし.summary: A local dish of the Nanyo area centered on Uwajima. Fresh sea bream sashimi is dipped in a soy-based sauce mixed with raw egg and placed on rice. It is said to have started as a dish eaten on boats by the fishermen of the Iyo navy. Adding sesame, nori and green onion enhances the flavor. The springy sea bream and mellow egg sauce go together well. Try it at restaurants in Uwajima. Some people save a little sauce to make ochazuke at the end.

shops.name: Kadoya Honten
shops.query: かどや 本店 宇和島
shops.comment: A taimeshi restaurant that began as a diner by Uwajima Station.

shops.name: Hozumitei
shops.query: ほづみ亭 宇和島
shops.comment: An Uwajima local-cuisine restaurant.

松山鯛めし.summary: Sea bream rice eaten in Matsuyama and the central and eastern parts of Ehime. A whole sea bream is cooked with rice in a clay pot. The fish's flavor and aroma soak into the rice for an elegant taste. Once cooked, the fish is flaked in front of you and mixed into the rice. It is fun that, even within Ehime, it is made completely differently from Uwajima's version. Try it at restaurants in Matsuyama and around Dogo Onsen. Watch out for bones.

shops.name: Matsuyama Taimeshi Akiyoshi
shops.query: 松山鯛めし 秋嘉 本店
shops.comment: Serves both Matsuyama and Uwajima styles of taimeshi.

shops.name: Goshiki Honten
shops.query: 郷土料理 五志喜 本店
shops.comment: A local-cuisine restaurant tracing its roots to the Edo period.

じゃこ天.summary: A fish cake famous in the Nanyo area of southern Ehime, such as Yawatahama and Uwajima. Small local fish are ground with bones and skin, shaped flat and fried. Because bones and skin are used, it is slightly grayish, with rich fish flavor and a firm bite. It is especially good piping hot. Eat it as is, or lightly toasted with ginger and soy sauce. It is sold at fish cake shops and souvenir stores, and it is perfect with drinks.

shops.name: Yasuoka Kamaboko
shops.query: 安岡蒲鉾 宇和島 じゃこ天
shops.comment: An Uwajima jakoten maker.

shops.name: Agora Marche
shops.query: アゴラマルシェ 八幡浜
shops.comment: Jakoten fried before your eyes.

鯛そうめん.summary: A local dish essential to celebrations in Ehime. A whole sea bream simmered sweet and savory is placed on a large platter, surrounded by colorful somen arranged like ocean waves. The noodles are dipped in the fish's simmering broth. Its gorgeous look has made it a feast at weddings and other celebrations. The broth soaked with sea bream flavor goes well with the smooth noodles. Try it at local restaurants in Matsuyama. Tai, sea bream, sounds like medetai, meaning auspicious.

shops.name: Goshiki Honten
shops.query: 郷土料理 五志喜 本店
shops.comment: A local-cuisine restaurant known for tai somen.

shops.name: Matsuyama Taimeshi Akiyoshi
shops.query: 松山鯛めし 秋嘉 本店
shops.comment: A sea bream specialist.

いもたき.summary: An autumn local dish said to have originated in Ozu, Ehime. Taro is the star, simmered with chicken, konnyaku, fried tofu and shiitake in a slightly sweet broth. In Ozu, many people gather on the banks of the Hiji River in autumn for imotaki parties, sharing pots while viewing the moon. Enjoy the soft, fluffy taro and flavorful broth. Gather around a pot on a long autumn night. The riverside event is a seasonal tradition locally.

shops.name: Ryoen Tarui
shops.query: 料苑たる井 大洲
shops.comment: A registered imotaki venue; enjoy it by the river from late summer into autumn.

shops.name: Yonezawa
shops.query: よねざわ 大洲 いもたき
shops.comment: A registered imotaki venue. Reservation required.

一六タルト.summary: One of Ehime's best-known sweets, made by a Matsuyama confectionery company. Yuzu-scented smooth bean paste is rolled in castella-like sponge like a roll cake. In Ehime, sweets rolled like this are called taruto. It is said to have started in the Edo period when a lord of the Matsuyama domain had one made based on a European sweet he encountered in Nagasaki. Enjoy the refreshing yuzu aroma and moist sponge. It is sold at Matsuyama Airport, stations and souvenir shops.

shops.name: Ichiroku Honpo Katsuyama
shops.query: 一六本舗 勝山本店
shops.comment: The flagship of a Meiji-era confectioner.

shops.name: Ichiroku Honpo Dogo
shops.query: 一六本舗 道後本館前店
shops.comment: Opposite Dogo Onsen Honkan.
shops.access: In front of Dogo Onsen Honkan

坊っちゃん団子.summary: A Matsuyama specialty named after a scene in Natsume Soseki's novel Botchan, in which the hero eats dango. Small mochi are coated in three kinds of bean paste, matcha, yellow and azuki, and skewered. They feature a colorful, cute look and a gentle sweetness. They are sold at many shops in Matsuyama, including around Dogo Onsen. Enjoy them with Japanese tea after a bath at Dogo Onsen. They are a popular souvenir. Savor them while imagining the world of the novel.

shops.name: Tsuboya Kashiho
shops.query: つぼや菓子舗 道後
shops.comment: A Dogo shop selling the original botchan dango.

shops.name: Utsuboya
shops.query: うつぼ屋 坊っちゃん団子
shops.comment: Also served as the tea sweet at Dogo Onsen Honkan.

母恵夢.summary: A popular souvenir sweet made by an Ehime confectionery company. Moist, castella-like dough rich with butter is wrapped around smooth white bean paste and baked. The name is said to carry the meaning of a dream of a mother's blessings. Like a Western-style bun, it is easy for children and adults to enjoy. It is also tasty warmed or chilled. It is widely sold at Matsuyama Airport, stations and souvenir shops. It goes well with tea or coffee.

shops.name: Poeme Sweets Park
shops.query: 母恵夢スイーツパーク
shops.comment: The factory shop at Poeme's headquarters.

shops.name: Matsuyama Airport souvenir shops
shops.query: 松山空港 おみやげ 母恵夢
shops.comment: Sold at the airport and station shops.

霧の森大福.summary: A matcha daifuku made in Shingu, Shikokuchuo. Using tea grown in Shingu, matcha-infused mochi wraps smooth bean paste and fresh cream, then is dusted generously with matcha. The balance of matcha's bitterness, mellow cream and sweet bean paste is superb. It is known as a popular, hard-to-get daifuku that often sells out at the shop in Shingu. Enjoy this luxurious taste from a tea-growing area. It does not keep long, so eat it soon.

shops.name: Kirinomori Kashi Kobo Shingu
shops.query: 霧の森菓子工房 新宮本店
shops.comment: The flagship of Kirinomori daifuku.

shops.name: Kirinomori Kashi Kobo Matsuyama
shops.query: 霧の森菓子工房 松山店
shops.comment: The Matsuyama shop; can sell out by midday.
